label: New Testament, Acts 2.22-36, especially 2.22…: Acts reports Peter's Pentecost speech: Jesus was a…
interpretation: 2.22: Jesus of Nazareth, 'a man attested (apodedeigmenon) by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did through him'; 2.24 and 2.32: God raised him, 'of which we are all witnesses'; 2.33: exalted at God's right hand, he received the promised Spirit from the Father and poured it out; 2.36: 'let all the house of Israel know assuredly (asphalōs) that God has made him both Lord and Christ'. Read as a report that the resurrection (with the signs) is presented as God's own act by which God makes known, so that it may be known assuredly, that Jesus holds a God-given office. Textual report only. Limits: the office named is 'Lord and Christ' and is said to be conferred ('made', epoiēsen) in connection with the exaltation, so the verse does not date the mandate to Jesus' ministry; it says nothing of founding a society or of a teaching commission. It supports STMT-RESURRECTION-CONFIRMS-JESUS-MANDATE more closely than Acts 17.31, whose appointment is to judge.
